facts: Q1 2026 total revenue was $13.4 million, down approximately 5% from $14.2 million in Q1 2025, driven by lower system capital sales which fell roughly $1.8 million year-over-year to about $800,000.
Recurring revenue grew 9% year-over-year to $12.6 million, representing 94% of total Q1 2026 revenue, with annualized recurring revenue running over $50 million.

LENSAR placed only 7 ALLY systems in the quarter (with 11 in backlog), bringing the ALLY installed base to approximately 205 and the total ALLY+LLS installed base to roughly 440, up 12% year-over-year.

The Alcon merger was terminated in mid-March 2026, and LENSAR recognized a $10 million acquisition deposit into other income upon termination (a non-cash recognition since funds were already in operating accounts).

Net income was $36.3 million ($1.56 per basic share) versus a net loss of $27.3 million a year ago, largely driven by non-cash items including a $23.9 million gain from change in fair value of warrant liabilities.

Q1 2026 procedure volume was approximately 54,000, up from 52,000 in Q1 2025 and 39,000 in Q1 2024, though management noted the year-over-year increase was solely from U.S. activity as OUS procedures were effectively flat.
U.S. procedure market share was 23.4% at quarter-end, flat versus December 31, reflecting fewer laser installations in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026.
Gross margin was 48% ($6.4 million) versus 50% in Q1 2025, within the previously guided 46%-49% range reflecting inflation and tariffs the company has chosen not to pass on to customers.
Adjusted EBITDA was negative $311,000 versus positive $165,000 a year ago, and the company ended the quarter with $13.5 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments.

CFO Tom Staab is departing after the call, and management indicated SG&A (excluding acquisition costs, which ran ~$6.9 million in both Q1 periods) will increase organically as LENSAR rebuilds service, application specialist, and sales personnel, with OUS shipments expected to resume this quarter following new distributor purchase orders.
Q4 2025 revenue was $4 million, a decrease of 20% compared to $5 million in Q4 2024.
Fiscal 2025 full-year revenue was $17.4 million compared to $20.6 million in 2024, a decrease of $3.2 million or 16%.
The company expects Q1 2026 consolidated revenues to be in the range of approximately $4.2 million to $4.5 million.
Management expects to achieve non-GAAP profitability in Q2 2026 and beyond.
The October 2025 strategic cost reductions resulted in savings of approximately $1.8 million per quarter ($7.2 million annualized) compared to Q2 2025.

CEO Bill Smith and his wife Dieva committed an additional $4 million in funding via a convertible note due March 2029, along with rolling $585,000 of previously outstanding notes into the same instrument.
The company plans to bring two new carrier customers to market by midyear 2026, both driven by SafePath OS product offerings.
Non-GAAP operating expenses declined 17% sequentially from Q3 to Q4 2025, and the company anticipates a further 5% decline in Q1 2026 versus Q4 2025.
Gross margin was 76.4% in Q4 2025, with the company targeting 78%-80% once full cost benefits are realized and a long-term gross margin target of 85%.
After 44 years as CEO, Bill Smith will transition to Executive Chairman effective March 31, 2026, with COO/CFO Tim Huffmyer becoming the new President and CEO.
EchoStar expects final regulatory approvals for its spectrum sale and the resulting influx of capital during the first half of 2026.

EchoStar's expected stake in SpaceX was approximately 2.8%, initially valued when SpaceX was at a $400 billion valuation, and the SpaceX-xAI merger appeared publicly to be structured at roughly an 80-20 split between xAI and Starlink.
EchoStar has stopped making payments to tower companies, citing a force majeure event triggered by the FCC's investigation to potentially take the company's spectrum.
EchoStar has settled hundreds of tower contracts with vendors who did not commence litigation, including a recent settlement with a large tower company.
EchoStar wrote off approximately $16 billion related to network decommissioning, including all operational costs.
The estimated remaining cash payments for taxes and decommissioning costs have been narrowed to $5 billion to $7 billion, down from an initial range of $7 billion to $10 billion.
EchoStar successfully moved all customers off its own network during Q4 2025.
Management stated the DISH Wireless business is very close to breakeven on an EBITDA basis but is not yet profitable.

Tower-related future commitment costs were accrued as part of the Q3 impairment charge and are therefore not reflected in Q4 numbers, while normal operating costs and noncash lease liability accretion continued through Q4.
EchoStar does not plan to hold a conference call after Q1 2026 and instead expects its next earnings call to be in July or early August 2026, after the second quarter, unless material changes occur.
Q3 FY2026 net sales were $667 million compared to $1.4 billion in the year-ago quarter, a decline of 53%.
Specialty eggs accounted for 50.5% of total shell egg sales in Q3 FY2026, up from 24.4% in the prior-year period, and Q3 specialty egg sales volumes were a record, up 5.8% year-over-year.
Prepared Foods sales were $63.6 million in Q3, up 441.2% year-over-year, and accounted for 9.5% of net sales compared to 0.8% a year ago.
Diluted earnings per share were $1.06 compared to $10.38 in the prior-year quarter, a decline of 89.8%, driven primarily by 56.5% lower shell egg selling prices.

The company expects Prepared Foods production capacity to increase more than 30% over the next 18 to 24 months through expansion projects at Echo Lake Foods, a new high-speed pancake line, and Crepini Foods' $7 million investment.

Approximately 12% of specialty egg pricing is tied to the cage-free California market, while the vast majority is under grain-based or fixed-price/cost-plus arrangements, supporting pricing stability.
The average layer flock is up approximately 2.2% year-over-year while HPAI-related depopulations are down 70.6% year-over-year, indicating meaningfully lower supply disruption.

The company ended the quarter with $1.152 billion in cash and temporary cash investments, remains virtually debt-free, and has $350.8 million remaining under its $500 million share repurchase authorization.

Over the trailing 12 months, the company allocated approximately $1 billion of capital: 38% ($384 million) to dividends, 30% ($299 million) to acquisitions, 17% ($117 million) to CapEx, and 15% ($150+ million) to share repurchases.

Q3 FY2026 Prepared Foods represents a trough quarter due to planned network optimization downtime and fixed-cost under-absorption, with management expecting progressive margin recovery beginning in Q4 FY2026 and trending back toward the 19-20% baseline through FY2027 and FY2028.
Q3 2025 revenue was $1.3 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by a 7% increase in real estate sales volume and a 3% increase in sales transactions.
Agent count was 83,446, down 2% year-over-year but up 1% quarter-over-quarter, marking the second consecutive quarter of sequential agent growth.
Sales transactions per agent increased 5.4% year-over-year, indicating improved agent productivity and success in attracting and retaining highly productive agents.
Adjusted EBITDA was $17.7 million for Q3, down year-over-year due to compressed gross margin partially offset by operational streamlining improvements.
The company ended the quarter with $112.8 million in cash on the balance sheet.
International revenue grew 68% year-over-year in Q3, and the international segment surpassed $100 million in revenue for the first time in a calendar year after just 9 months.
GAAP gross margin was 6.5%, down 57 basis points from Q3 last year, as more productive agents are hitting their commission cap.
Worldwide agent attrition improved 13% year-over-year, and U.S. agent attrition improved 18% year-over-year.
G&A expenses decreased to $82 million in Q3 from $89 million in Q2, with transaction processing unit costs falling from approximately $621 in Q2 to $523 in Q3.
39% of new agents joining eXp in Q3 were on teams, and agents on teams are 79% more productive than individual agents.
Q3 2026 consolidated net sales increased 3.1% to $235.7 million, including $23.1 million from Saxdor, with legacy net sales of $212.6 million exceeding the guidance range of $198–$202 million.

Legacy unit volume decreased 17.1% to 1,187 units due to disciplined wholesale shipments, while legacy net sales per unit increased 12.1% to $179,000; Saxdor contributed 66 units at an ASP of $350,000.

Gross margin was 17.5%, compressing 250 basis points year-over-year due to fixed cost deleverage and higher per-unit costs, but expanded 420 basis points sequentially from Q2 reflecting centralized sourcing benefits.

Adjusted EBITDA was $22.7 million (9.6% margin), including approximately $1.4 million from one month of Saxdor contribution; GAAP net loss was $2.4 million versus net income of $13.2 million prior year, largely driven by $10.6 million of acquisition/integration expenses.

Full-year fiscal 2026 combined guidance is net sales of $880–$886 million and adjusted EBITDA of $72–$74 million, with legacy revenue now expected to be down only slightly versus FY2025 (improved from flat to down mid-single digits).

Q4 guidance calls for consolidated net sales of $261–$267 million and adjusted EBITDA of $29–$31 million (11–12% margin), with Saxdor expected to contribute $57–$59 million at 10–11% margin during its European peak season.
Legacy full-year adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to finish at the lower end of the previously communicated 8–9% range, as Q3's favorable mix tailwind is not expected to repeat in Q4.

The Saxdor acquisition closed on March 2, financed partially with ~1.5 million shares issued at a deal-priced VWAP of $30.98 (GAAP fair value $27.37), leaving pro forma leverage at ~1.5x net debt/EBITDA versus the 2.5x maximum target.

The company repurchased approximately 492,000 shares at an average price of $26.24 during the quarter, with the $70 million share repurchase authorization remaining in effect; free cash flow was $16 million on $5.9 million of capex.

Saxdor's new 460 GTC flagship has its full planned production for the year effectively sold out, and the Fort Pierce facility operates at ~65% utilization, providing capacity to expand Saxdor's North American production without greenfield investment.
Net sales for Q1 fiscal 2026 increased 8.1% to $298.7 million compared to $276.2 million in Q1 fiscal 2025.
Diluted earnings per share improved 59% to $1.59 compared to $1.00 in the prior year first quarter.
The Board approved a special cash dividend of $1 per share, returning approximately $11.7 million to stockholders, payable on December 30, 2025.
Gross profit increased $7.6 million or 16.2% to $54.1 million, with gross profit margin improving to 18.1% from 16.9%.
Total operating expenses as a percentage of net sales decreased to 9.1% from 10.7% in the prior year quarter.
The weighted average cost per pound of raw nut and dry fruit increased 24.8% year-over-year due to higher commodity acquisition costs for all major tree nuts.
Total inventory value increased $40.2 million or 20.6% compared to the prior year quarter due to higher commodity costs and greater finished goods quantities.
Sales volume in the commercial ingredients distribution channel increased 12.8%, while contract manufacturing channel volume increased 18.4%.
Consumer distribution channel sales volume decreased 5.1%, with private brand sales volume down 3.2%, partly due to peanut butter discontinuation at a mass merchandiser.
Orchard Valley Harvest brand pound shipments decreased 44%, driven by discontinuation at a national specialty retailer.
Q1 2026 revenue was $231.3 million, up 34.2% year-over-year, with gross margin of 46.5%, above the midpoint of the 42%-48% long-term target range.

ECP, front-end packaging, furnace and other technologies revenue surged 204.9% to $84.2 million (36.4% of sales), while single-wafer cleaning/Tahoe/semi-critical cleaning revenue fell 5.5% to $122.5 million (53% of sales).
Advanced packaging revenue (excluding ECP) grew 62% to $24.5 million, representing 10.6% of sales.
Q1 shipments rose 53.6% to $240.7 million, with about 15% representing catch-up from tools originally scheduled for Q4 2025 delivery; cleaning shipments alone grew 32%.
Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $1.08–$1.175 billion (implying ~25% growth at midpoint) and expects shipment growth to outpace revenue growth in 2026.

The company expects to deliver 15-20 single-wafer SPM tools by year-end across its customer base, with proprietary technology achieving <15 particles at 15nm (better than the market leader) in a market segment representing 30% of cleaning.
Operating margin compressed to 18.1% from 20.7%, with operating expenses up 38.5% to $65.8 million and non-GAAP EPS falling to $0.34 from $0.46.
Cash, equivalents and time deposits totaled $1.25 billion with net cash of $924.2 million, boosted by $110 million in gross proceeds from a February sale of ACM Shanghai shares.
Inventory rose to $738 million (raw materials up $28.3M QoQ to $377.9M), cash used in operations was $29.5 million, and full-year 2026 capex is now expected at approximately $175 million.

By year-end 2026, ACM expects to have more than 20 tools installed outside Mainland China across about 10 customers in 5 countries, with Oregon U.S.-made tool production capability targeted by year-end 2026 and the second Lingang building opening later this year (supporting up to $3 billion in annual output).
HealthStream achieved record quarterly revenues of $76.5 million in Q3 2025, up 4.6% year-over-year, with operating income up 16.5%, net income up 6.3%, and adjusted EBITDA up 7.9%.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a record high of $19.1 million with a margin of 25%, compared to 24.2% in the prior year quarter.
CredentialStream revenue grew 23%, ShiftWizard grew 29%, and Competency Suite grew 18% compared to Q3 2024.

Remaining performance obligations were $621 million at quarter end compared to $549 million in the same period last year, with approximately 39% expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months.
The company completed its $25 million share repurchase program, repurchasing $6.9 million of common stock in Q3 2025.
HealthStream acquired Virsys12 on October 8 for $11.2 million in cash, with up to an additional $4 million contingent on achieving certain financial targets over three years.

Full year 2025 revenue guidance was narrowed to $299.5 million to $301.5 million, including approximately $900,000 contribution from Virsys12 offset by an expected $3 million decline in legacy credentialing and scheduling products.
The company ended Q3 with cash and investment balances of $92.6 million and no interest-bearing debt.
NurseGrid now has over 660,000 monthly active users with approximately 2,000 new subscribers added organically each week.
Legacy credentialing and scheduling application revenues declined by $1.7 million compared to last year, but excluding legacy products, the core business grew 8%.
DT Midstream delivered Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $308 million, a $15 million increase from the prior quarter, with the Pipeline segment up $14 million and Gathering up $1 million.

DTM reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range and 2027 early outlook, and expects Q2 2026 to be lower than Q1 due to interstate pipeline seasonality, a Guardian Pipeline rate step-down, and planned maintenance.
The Board approved a Q1 dividend of $0.88 per share, unchanged from the prior quarter, with commitment to grow the dividend in line with adjusted EBITDA.

DTM approved a Vector Pipeline mainline expansion adding ~400 MMcf/d of capacity, anchored by investment-grade utility customers under 20-year negotiated rate contracts, with Q4 2028 in-service and total DTM investment of $80–$100 million.
DTM approved the Millennium R2R project, supported by long-term contracts with two utilities and an existing power plant for 70 MMcf/d, expected fully in service in Q1 2027.

Committed capital was increased to approximately $400 million for 2026 and approximately $440 million for 2027 to reflect the new Vector and Millennium R2R investments, with Q1 2026 growth capex of $72 million.

DTM signed an agreement to build a lateral off Midwestern Pipeline for a 900 MW power plant in Indiana under a 20-year demand-based contract for ~265 MMcf/d, contingent on customer FID expected in 2026, with in-service in 1H 2028.

Midwestern Pipeline's nonbinding open season for up to 1.5 Bcf/d of northbound and southbound expansion capacity was oversubscribed, and Vector's 2030 westbound expansion open season for 300–500 MMcf/d into Chicago was also oversubscribed.

A new 250 MMcf/d interconnect was commercialized on NEXUS to supply a behind-the-meter gas-fired power generation facility serving an Ohio data center, and Midwestern recontracted ~30% of system capacity with term extensions of 5 to 25 years.

LEAP pipeline is running full at its 2.1 Bcf/d design capacity with expansion potential to 4 Bcf/d via pipe and compression, Haynesville volumes averaged 2.09 Bcf/d and Northeast volumes averaged 1.42 Bcf/d in Q1, and management cited a $3.4 billion project backlog with Moody's raising the off-balance-sheet leverage ceiling to 4.25x.
Driven Brands delivered Q3 2025 revenue growth of 7% and adjusted EBITDA of $136 million, with same-store sales up 2.8% marking the 19th consecutive quarter of positive same-store sales.
Take 5 Oil Change achieved its 21st consecutive quarter of same-store sales growth at 6.8%, with system-wide sales growing 18% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA growth of 15%.
Take 5 now represents more than 75% of Driven's overall adjusted EBITDA, with trailing 12-month system-wide sales of $1.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA of over $400 million.
Non-oil change revenue now accounts for more than 25% of Take 5 sales, with attachment rates for non-oil change services growing from the mid-40s to the low-50s over the past 24 months.
Net leverage was reduced to 3.8x from 4.1x at the end of Q2 2025, with the company repaying approximately $486 million of debt year-to-date through Q3.
The company narrowed full-year 2025 guidance to revenue of $2.1 billion to $2.12 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $525 million to $535 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.23 to $1.28.
Following the October refinancing, Driven's debt is now 92% fixed rate with a weighted average interest rate of 4.4%, and full year interest expense is expected to be approximately $120 million.
The Franchise segment delivered adjusted EBITDA margins of 66% in Q3, an improvement of 90 basis points versus the prior year.
Take 5's new unit pipeline remains robust with approximately 900 locations at the end of Q3, of which over one-third are sites secured or further along in development.

Management cited Q4 choppiness across the portfolio due to macroeconomic uncertainty including the government shutdown, indicating same-store sales will come in at the low end of the original 1% to 3% guidance range.
Revenue for Q3 FY2026 was $45.6 million, representing 5% year-over-year organic growth and 8% growth including acquisitions.
Music Publishing revenue increased 12% year-over-year to $30.1 million, driven by performance revenue from hit songs and Digital revenue growth.
Recorded Music revenue increased 8% year-over-year to $12.9 million, benefiting from streaming growth and catalog acquisitions.
OIBDA increased 11% year-over-year to $18.1 million, while adjusted EBITDA also rose 11% year-over-year to $19.2 million.
Net income decreased to $2.2 million from $5.3 million in the prior year quarter, primarily due to a loss on fair value of swaps and increased interest expense.
Interest expense increased by $800,000 year-over-year to $6.6 million due to higher borrowings to support M&A strategy, partially offset by lower interest rates.
Cash flows from operating activities increased by $5.1 million year-over-year to $38.2 million.
Total liquidity stood at $114.8 million, consisting of $20.6 million cash and $94.2 million available under the revolver, with net debt of $431.7 million compared to $366.7 million at March 31, 2025.
Full year FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $170-$173 million from $167-$170 million, implying 8% growth at midpoint versus FY2025.
Full year FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $71.5-$73.5 million from $70-$72 million, signaling more than 10% growth over the prior year at midpoint.
Full year 2025 sales were $2.1 billion with operating income of $287 million and earnings per share of $5.52.
Operating margin declined to 13.9% from 14.9% in the prior year, with lower volume accounting for approximately 80 basis points of the decline.
Sales of the company's newest products accounted for 19% of total sales, the highest level ever achieved.
The Engineered Solutions segment delivered record operating income of $163 million and record operating margin of 16.7% of sales.
Cat litter sales were 7% higher in the second half of 2025 compared to the first half, and the company secured approximately $25-30 million in new pet litter business starting Q2 2026.
Full year sales into edible oil and renewable fuel purification grew 17% and animal feed additives sales grew 12%.
The company returned $73 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, with approximately $140 million remaining on the share repurchase authorization.
Free cash flow was $87 million for the year, and management expects 2026 free cash flow in the 6% to 7% of sales range.
The balance sheet ended the year with more than $700 million in liquidity and a net leverage ratio of 1.7x EBITDA.

Management expects Q1 2026 sales and operating income to be similar to Q4, representing approximately 5% growth over the prior year, with $50 million of new revenue from growth investments and $20 million from pricing expected in 2026.
Third quarter adjusted earnings were $1 billion or $2.52 per share, with operating cash flow excluding working capital of $1.9 billion.
Refining achieved 99% utilization in Q3, the highest quarter since 2018, with a record year-to-date clean product yield of 87%.
The company is targeting adjusted controllable cost per barrel of approximately $5.50 on an annual basis by 2027, compared to $6.07 in Q3 (which included a $0.40 per barrel environmental accrual).
Net debt to capital was 41%, with a debt reduction target of $17 billion by end of 2027, supported by expected working capital benefit of approximately $1.5 billion in Q4.
Year-to-date adjusted chemicals EBITDA was $700 million, with chemicals operating above 100% utilization despite challenging market conditions.
Midstream EBITDA target is $4.5 billion by year-end 2027, with Q3 annualized run rate approaching $4 billion.
The company returned $751 million to shareholders in Q3, including $267 million in share repurchases, maintaining commitment to return at least 50% of operating cash flow.
The WRB acquisition adds 250,000 barrels per day of processing capacity, with a cross-functional team identifying 30-plus synergy initiatives.
Western Gateway refined products pipeline announced as a 50-50 partnership with Kinder Morgan, with capital spend expected in the 2027-2029 timeframe.
Q4 guidance includes worldwide crude utilization in the low to mid-90s and turnaround expense between $125 million and $145 million, reflecting 100% WRB ownership and removal of Los Angeles refinery.
Full year record EBITDA increased 200% to over $1 billion, and full year free cash flow increased to $666 million versus negative $9 million in 2024.
Year-end cash increased more than 10x to $554 million, and net income increased tenfold to a record $586 million.

The combined company with New Gold is expected to generate approximately $3 billion of EBITDA and $2 billion of free cash flow on a full year run rate basis based on consensus commodity prices from last October.
Las Chispas generated $286 million of free cash flow in only 10.5 months of contribution, finishing the year as the top cash flow generator.
Total debt declined $250 million or 42% year-over-year, with total liquidity nearing $1 billion.
Gold and silver reserves grew by 10% after replacing depletion, and inferred resources grew by 40% across the portfolio, including a 216% increase at Wharf and an 86% increase at Palmarejo.

Wharf's mine life nearly doubled to 12 years with 500,000 ounces of gold reserves and 1 million ounces of inferred resources added, while Palmarejo's mine life was extended by 5 years with reserves increasing almost 40% to 2 million gold equivalent ounces.

Silver is expected to contribute approximately 42% of total 2026 revenue based on current prices and midpoint of guidance, up from about 35% in 2025, with a 10% expected year-over-year increase in silver production.
Return on invested capital was a peer-leading 26% in 2025, and the company plans to announce a robust update to its return of capital strategy upon closing of the New Gold transaction.

Total exploration investment is expected to increase to between $120 million and $136 million in 2026, a 47% increase compared to 2025 levels, with approximately 80% of cash taxes expected to be paid in Mexico.
Evergy reported Q3 2025 adjusted earnings of $2.03 per share compared to $2.02 per share in Q3 2024.
The company narrowed its 2025 adjusted EPS guidance range to $3.92 to $4.02 per share from the original range of $3.92 to $4.12 per share.
Below normal cooling degree days in Q2 and Q3 negatively impacted results by $0.13 per share, with mitigation efforts offsetting approximately $0.10 per share.
Evergy announced a 4% increase in its quarterly dividend to $2.78 per share on an annualized basis.
The company's economic development pipeline exceeds 15 gigawatts, with a Tier 1 large customer load opportunity of 4 to 6 gigawatts.
Lambda announced plans for a data center in Kansas City, Missouri expected to launch in early 2026 with 24 megawatts of capacity and potential to scale to over 100 megawatts.
Weather-normalized demand increased by 2% in Q3 2025 compared to the prior year.
Evergy's current 5-year capital plan totals $17.5 billion with corresponding 8.5% rate base growth through 2029.

The company's current load growth forecast of 2% to 3% annually through 2029 could increase to 4% to 5% CAGR if final agreements are reached with two data center customers representing approximately 600 megawatts by 2029.

Evergy expects to fund its capital plan with up to $2.8 billion of equity and equity content instruments, though management noted potential to reduce equity needs by hundreds of millions of dollars as large load customer cash flows materialize.

The North America ERP go-live in the first week of November 2025 resulted in 3 full weeks of lost machine order entry and parts shipping capability, reducing Q4 net sales by an estimated $30 million and Q4 adjusted EBITDA by approximately $22 million.
Total ERP program investment since 2023 has reached approximately $98 million, and 2026 ERP-related spending is now expected to exceed $20 million, up from the originally planned ~$5 million.
Full year 2025 consolidated net sales were $1,203.5 million, a 6.5% decrease from $1,286.7 million in 2024, with organic sales declining 7.3% on a constant currency basis.
The company's autonomous mobile robot (AMR) portfolio delivered roughly $85 million in sales in 2025, and management set a revenue target of approximately $250 million in AMR revenue by 2028.
In 2025, the company repurchased approximately 1.1 million shares for $88.5 million, reducing outstanding shares by about 6%, and increased its annual dividend for the 54th consecutive year.
Full year 2025 adjusted EPS was $4.57 per diluted share, down from $6.57 in 2024, while 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is $4.70 to $5.30 per diluted share.
For 2026, Tennant projects net sales of $1.24 billion to $1.28 billion, reflecting organic sales growth of 3% to 6.5%, with adjusted EBITDA guided to $175 million to $190 million.

A comprehensive physical inventory requiring a 2-week shutdown of U.S. manufacturing and distribution facilities in early January 2026 will significantly affect Q1 sales and costs, with results heavily weighted toward the back half of 2026.
The EMEA ERP go-live timeline has been paused with no new date set, as the company redirects 100% of its focus to North America recovery.
The company recorded $6.4 million in restructuring charges for a global workforce reorganization and expects approximately $10 million in annual savings beginning in 2026.

Q4 2025 revenue of $5.3 billion grew 3.8% year-over-year in constant currency (all organic), with full year revenue of $21.1 billion growing 6.4% in constant currency and surpassing the $20 billion mark.
Financial Services led growth with Q4 constant currency revenue increasing 9% year-over-year and 7% for the full year, the highest annual level since 2016.

Q4 bookings grew 9% year-on-year to a record quarterly total contract value, with 12 large deals of $100 million or greater TCV including one deal valued at more than $1 billion, and large deal wins value 60% greater than a year ago.
The company signed 28 deals with TCV above $100 million in 2025, with combined TCV up nearly 50% versus last year, including 5 mega deals with TCV of $500 million or greater.
Q4 adjusted operating margin of 16% improved 30 basis points year-over-year, with full year adjusted operating margin of 15.8% rising 50 basis points over last year and exceeding guidance.
Full year 2025 adjusted diluted EPS of $5.28 grew 11% year-over-year, with Q4 adjusted diluted EPS of $1.35 up 12% year-over-year.
Full year 2025 free cash flow was approximately $2.7 billion, representing more than 100% of net income.

The company returned approximately $2 billion to shareholders in 2025 through dividends and share repurchases, and plans to return approximately $1.6 billion in 2026 including approximately $1 billion in share repurchases.

For 2026, the company guided revenue growth of 4% to 6.5% in constant currency (including approximately 150 basis points inorganic), adjusted operating margin of 15.9% to 16.1%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $5.56 to $5.70 representing 5% to 8% growth.

Over 30% of developer effort in software development cycles is now AI-assisted and agentic, while fixed bid and transaction-based work now represents more than 50% of revenue compared to 41-42% three years ago.
Lincoln National delivered its fifth consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth in adjusted operating income, reporting $397 million or $2.04 per share for Q3 2025.
Annuity sales reached $4.5 billion in Q3, the fourth consecutive quarter of increased sales, with spread-based products (fixed annuities and RILA) representing 63% of new business.
Fixed annuity sales increased 36% year-over-year while RILA sales increased 21% year-over-year, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of sequential RILA growth.
Group Protection premium grew 5% year-over-year with supplemental health premiums increasing 33% year-over-year, and sales grew nearly 40% year-over-year.
The company expects full year Group Protection margin in the mid- to upper 8% range, representing approximately 50 basis points improvement year-over-year.
Retirement Plan Services achieved first year sales of $2.4 billion with total deposits increasing 20% year-over-year and positive net flows of $755 million.
Lincoln fully transitioned to retaining 100% of fixed annuity sales during the quarter, exiting its external flow reinsurance agreement.
The company completed $1.9 billion in funding agreement-backed note (FABN) issuance year-to-date as part of its institutional funding agreement program.
The Group Protection disability loss ratio increased to 76.7% from 70.5% in Q3 2024, driven by lower LTD recoveries and one month of unfavorable severity.
The investment portfolio maintained strong credit quality with 97% of investments rated investment grade and below investment grade exposure near historic lows.
Adjusted earnings per diluted share increased 15.3% year-over-year to $2.49 in Q3 2025, with the assumption update contributing $0.76 to EPS.
Remeasurement gains on reserves totaled $580 million in the quarter, reducing benefits and increasing the deferred profit liability by $55 million.
Japan's pretax margin reached 52.2% in Q3, up 750 basis points year-over-year, driven notably by the unlock of actuarial assumptions.
Japan's third sector benefit ratio declined approximately 14 percentage points year-over-year to 27.8% for the quarter.
The company repurchased $1 billion of its own stock and paid dividends of $309 million in Q3 2025.
Unencumbered holding company liquidity stood at $4.5 billion, which was $2.7 billion above the minimum balance requirement.
The company enhanced liquidity and capital flexibility by $2 billion through the creation of two off-balance sheet pre-capitalized trusts (PCAPs).
CECL reserves for the commercial real estate portfolio increased by $28 million net of charge-offs due to continued distressed property values.
